---
title: cast_hier2dim
---
## Cast Hierarchical List into Dimensional list {.unnumbered}


### Description

<code>cast_hier2dim()</code> casts a hierarchical list into a dimensional list
(i.e. into a recursive array). <br />
<code>hier2dim()</code> takes a hierarchical list,
and predicts what dimensions the list would have,
if re-casted by the <code>cast_hier2dim()</code> function. <br />
<br />



### Usage

<pre><code class='language-R'>cast_hier2dim(x, ...)

hier2dim(x, ...)

## Default S3 method:
cast_hier2dim(x, in2out = TRUE, maxdepth = 16L, recurse_classed = FALSE, ...)

## Default S3 method:
hier2dim(x, in2out = TRUE, maxdepth = 16L, recurse_classed = FALSE, ...)
</code></pre>


### Arguments

<table>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="x">x</code></td>
<td>
a list. <br />
If <code>x</code> has redundant nesting,
it is advisable (though not necessary) to reduce the redundant nesting using [dropnests](dropnests.qmd).
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="...">...</code></td>
<td>
further arguments passed to or from methods. <br /> <br />
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="in2out">in2out</code></td>
<td>
see broadcast_casting.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="maxdepth">maxdepth</code></td>
<td>
a single, positive integer, giving the maximum depth to drop nesting in. <br />
The surface-level elements of a list is depth 1, so <code>maxdepth</code> must be <code style="white-space: pre;">&gt;= 2</code>.
</td></tr>
<tr><td style = "white-space: collapse; font-family: monospace; vertical-align: top"><code id="recurse_classed">recurse_classed</code></td>
<td>
<code>TRUE</code> or <code>FALSE</code>,
indicating if the function should also recurse through classed lists within <code>x</code>,
like data.frames.
</td></tr>
</table>


### Value

For <code>cast_hier2dim()</code>: <br />
A recursive array (i.e. a dimensional list). <br />
<br />
For <code>hier2dim()</code>: <br />
An integer vector,
giving the dimensions <code>x</code> would have,
if re-casted by <code>cast_hier2dim()</code>. <br />
<br />



### Examples
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, eval=TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = NA}
library("broadcast")


# ideal scenario ====
x <- list(
  group1 = list(
    id1 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    ),
    id2 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    ),
    id3 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    )
  ),
  group2 = list(
    id1 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    ),
    id2 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    ),
    id3 = list(
      height = rnorm(10, 170),
      weight = rnorm(10, 80),
      sex = sample(c("M", "F", NA), 10, TRUE)
    )
  )
)

print(x)

hier2dim(x) # predict what dimensions `x` would have if casted as dimensional
x2 <- cast_hier2dim(x) # cast as dimensional

# since the original list uses the same names for all elements within the same depth,
# dimnames can be set easily:
dimnames(x2) <- list(
  names( x[[1]][[1]] ),
  names( x[[1]] ),
  names( x )
)
print(x2) # very compact, maybe too compact...?

# print a small portion of the list, but less compact:
cast_dim2flat(x2[, 1:2, "group1", drop = FALSE])




```
